quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: What does alcohol do?

options.text: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain and reduces skills needed for safe driving. It causes slower reactions and poor judgment.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must turn right or left.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must turn right or left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a Y intersection ahead. You must turn either right or left.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:
questions.explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol harm your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle when:

options.text: A traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, red lights, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:

options.text: Sit in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your hazard flashers and move off the road as far as possible. Lift your hood so other drivers know your car is disabled.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your car in reverse to go back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn if you miss your exit. Go to the next exit instead.

questions.question: Aggressive drivers:

options.text: Take out their frustrations on other motorists.
Run stop signs, speed, tailgate, weave in and out of traffic, and make unsafe lane changes.

questions.explanation: Aggressive drivers engage in risky behavior. They run stop signs, speed, tailgate, weave in and out of traffic, make unsafe lane changes, and honk or gesture angrily.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but harms judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It has no effect on either one.
It harms driving skills but not judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, impairs your vision, and harms your judgment of speed and distance. It also makes you more likely to take dangerous risks.

questions.question: Drivers must make sure children are properly secured in vehicles.
questions.explanation: Drivers must ensure all passengers under 18 are properly secured with a safety belt, booster seat, or child safety seat, regardless of where they sit in the vehicle.

questions.question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.explanation: When leaving your vehicle, turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.

questions.explanation: Drivers must make about 200 decisions for every mile they drive. Any extra task can distract you from driving safely.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: You should change your driving when weather changes suddenly.
You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch carefully for vehicles behind you in bad weather.

questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Slow down in rain and fog. Watch for vehicles behind you that may be driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: How should you change lanes?

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot where you plan to move, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot where you plan to move, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Signal first, then check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to see your blind spot. Make sure no one is in the lane you want to enter. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Wait for your body to process the alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Only time will lower your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot reduce your BAC or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they do not change your BAC.

questions.question: When you see a green light, what should you do?

options.text: Keep going, unless there are vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep going, unless there are vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, let pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection pass first. You can go through, but drive at a speed where you can stop if the light changes.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Do not stand in traffic lanes because another vehicle could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: This sign is a:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to hazards or special situations ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They prepare you for road hazards ahead. This sign tells you there is a stop sign coming. Be ready to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop when reacting to other drivers' unexpected moves.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances. You need more time and space to stop when driving fast.

questions.question: Because driving has risks, you should always try to improve your driving and observation skills.
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires constant improvement. Always work on your driving and observation skills for your safety and the safety of others.

questions.question: Before starting the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have their seat belts on.
Make sure only adults have their seat belts on.
Make sure only children have their seat belts on.
Make sure all passengers have their seat belts on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have their seat belts on.
questions.explanation: Create a safe habit each time you enter and leave your car. Before starting the engine, buckle your seat belt. Make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: The most common mistake drivers make when backing up is not looking both ways behind the car.
questions.explanation: Drivers often fail to look both ways when backing up. Your mirrors do not show everything behind you. Turn your body and head to look through the rear window to see as much as possible.

questions.question: How lack of sleep affects your driving is similar to:

options.text: How driving with teenagers affects driving.

questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol have the same effects on safe driving. Being awake for 18 hours impairs driving as much as a 0.05 percent blood alcohol level. Being awake for 24 hours straight affects driving the same as a 0.10 percent blood alcohol level.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers what rules they must follow. When you see this sign, U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Drivers who drink alcohol before driving:

options.text: Always know the risks they are taking.
Cannot control their body, mind, or the car properly.
Are better drivers because they are more careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot control their body, mind, or the car properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your thinking, vision, focus, and reaction time. It is never safe to drink any amount of alcohol before driving.

questions.question: This is a ____ sign.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign is a Yield sign. When you see it, slow down and check for traffic. Let pedestrians and other cars cross first. Only stop if necessary.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you must:

options.text: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and other traffic.
Stop completely and wait for a green light.
Slow down and look for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and other traffic.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign is a Stop sign. You must come to a complete stop. Look for pedestrians and cars crossing. Wait until the intersection is clear before going.

questions.question: You cannot pass a school bus when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, you must stop before you reach it. Stay stopped until the lights stop flashing. On roads with a center divider, cars on the opposite side may not need to stop.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic light is coming. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on the upcoming hill.
Trucks are on the upcoming hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a steep hill or downgrade ahead.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the wheel straight and slow down by lifting your foot off the gas pedal.
Keep your speed the same and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel straight and slow down by lifting your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the car going straight. Take your foot off the gas pedal and do not brake until you have control of the car. Once the car is under control, brake gently and pull safely off the road.

questions.question: You are legally intoxicated if your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is at least:
questions.explanation: If you are 21 or older, you are considered to be driving under the influence if your BAC is 0.08 percent or higher. Even with a BAC below 0.08 percent, you can still be charged with driving under the influence if your driving is impaired.

questions.question: What does this sign prevent?

options.text: Cars from entering full parking lots.
Cars from entering road construction areas.
Cars from entering one-way streets and expressway ramps from the wrong direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars from entering one-way streets and expressway ramps from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road is one-way traffic. You cannot enter from your current direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep driving at your current speed.

questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?

options.text: Snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
So the buzzer or light stops working.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should fit comfortably so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.
